International Graduate Student FAQs
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for International Graduate Students
Below you'll find the most common questions for international students applying for
graduate admissions at Binghamton University.
Graduate Applicant Questions
What are Binghamton's application requirements?
Binghamton University has general application requirements for all students. International applicants also have additional requirements that
can be found on our international student requirements webpage.
How do I obtain information about a specific program?
To receive more detailed information about an academic program at Binghamton via email,
contact the Office of Graduate Admissions at gradadmission@binghamton.edu.
What are Binghamton's English language requirements for international students?
All international students applying to Binghamton University must show proof of English
proficiency. More information can be found under the "Proof of English Proficiency"
section on the international student requirements page.
What financial aid and funding are available for international students?
Binghamton University offers numerous funding options. From loans, fellowships, assistantships, and scholarships to student employment and travel funding, Binghamton can help you find the sources
you need to enhance your career and make your education attainable.
Does the admissions committee have access to my financial documents?
No, the graduate admissions committee does not have access to your financial documents and holistically makes admission and funding
decisions based on merit alone.
How much does it cost to attend Binghamton University?
You can find in-state, out-of-state, and international graduate student pricing information
on our Cost of Attendance page.
Can I apply for more than one graduate degree at Binghamton?
Yes, Binghamton University offers students in select programs the opportunity to work
toward earning two master's degrees (dual degrees) at the same time. This allows students to earn two master's degrees in just three
years, saving both time and money.
Is there an application fee?
Yes, the application fee is $75 (USD) and is non-refundable.
Does Binghamton offer an application fee waiver?
Yes, some students may be eligible for an application fee waiver:
Academic departments may periodically offer application fee waivers dependent upon
students' academic eligibility, enrollment needs of the department and other extraordinary
situations. Prior to any possible departmental consideration, applicants should begin
their application and submit minimally their transcripts, personal statement and resume.
After uploading these documents, outreach to program recruiters may be sought.
Note: A request for an application fee waiver may take some time. Before submitting
your application, wait for an email stating that your request has been approved. If
you have any questions about this process, contact us at gradadmission@binghamton.edu.
What is the application deadline for Binghamton?
Most programs review applications on a rolling basis rather than after a set deadline,
meaning we continue to make admission decisions until the program is full. Most programs
have their deadline as January 15, although some program deadlines may vary. Check
our Graduate Admission Requirements page and select your degree for specific program deadlines.
How do I find out the status of my application materials?
You can check the status of your application through our online portal and see what items were received and what still needs to be submitted.
Graduate Admitted Student Questions
What are the next steps once you've been admitted to Binghamton's Graduate School?
If you have been admitted to Binghamton University, next steps will be sent to you
by email.
Will there be an orientation for new students?
Yes, Binghamton University will host an orientation for new students. Visit the International Student Scholar Services (ISSS) website for Orientation information.
How do I register for courses?
Binghamton graduate students will receive information from their academic departments
regarding course registrations. Until then, we encourage you to explore course offerings on our website.
How do I review courses and course descriptions for my program?
Required courses and course descriptions can be found in the Binghamton Academic Guide.
How will I be billed at Binghamton?
Binghamton University has partnered with Flywire to streamline the tuition payment process for our international students. With Flywire,
making an international payment is fast, simple and cost-effective. In most cases,
you can pay in your home currency and benefit from excellent foreign exchange rates.
How many credits can I take per semester at Binghamton?
The minimum course load for new graduate students is 12 credits per semester. After
completion of 24 credits, the minimum course load drops to 9 credits.
Federal regulations require that students in F-1 and J-1 status be registered for
a full-time course load each fall and spring semester until graduation. Failure to be registered as a full-time
student is a violation of your non-immigrant status, resulting in the loss of F-1
or J-1 benefits (including employment eligibility both on and off campus) and may
subject you to federal immigration sanctions.
Where can I find information about housing at Binghamton?
Off-Campus College (OCC) provides a database that contains apartments and rooms for rent, as well as a roommate
registry. The housing and roommate search features are available to the Binghamton
University community through the use of their University email.
Who do I contact for parking permits or public transportation information?
Students can purchase parking permits online. A vehicle must be registered with the University before parking on campus or it
must be parked in a paid space. Public transportation is free with your University
ID through the Binghamton city bus service and through the student-run Off-Campus College.
Is health insurance offered at Binghamton?
Yes. In accordance with federal immigration policy and the State University of New
York (SUNY), appropriate and sufficient health insurance is a mandatory requirement
for all international students enrolled at a SUNY campus. Health insurance coverage for accompanying family members is a mandatory requirement for J-2 family members
and is available to other non-immigrant visa holders as well.
Can I defer my admission to Binghamton?
If the graduate program approves an applicant's deferral, the program should submit
an admission deferral request to the Office of Graduate Recruitment and Admissions,
who will review the request and either approve or deny it.
If difficulty in obtaining a visa prevents an international applicant from enrolling
in the semester specified in the acceptance letter, the applicant should contact the
graduate program directly. The graduate program will then advise the Office of Graduate
Recruitment and Admissions of the applicant's status.
How do I obtain an I-20 or DS-2019 form?
Applicants to the Binghamton University Graduate School who are citizens of other
countries, whether they are enrolled in a school in the United States or abroad, are
required to meet academic standards for admission to a degree program, show proficiency in English
at the college level, and certify that they will have the required amount of money
needed for each year of study. When applicants are admitted to Binghamton University,
the Office of International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS) issues a Certificate
of Eligibility as either Form I-20 (F-1 visa) or Form DS-2019 (J-1 visa). Detailed
information on required materials can be found on the Additional Application Requirements for International Students webpage.
